findings.rationale: Literate input is written with std::fs::write to a predictable PID-derived sibling path. A stale or pre-created symlink at that path is followed and overwritten, and PID reuse can also collide with stale materializations. Use an exclusively created randomized temporary file and retain its handle.

Migration plans and semantic checks are computed from earlier file contents, but the commit phase verifies only that each target is still a regular file. If a target changes before rename, the validated replacement silently overwrites the newer contents; the backup merely preserves the already-changed file for error rollback and does not prevent successful data loss.

Document generation verifies signed approval records against trust keys, but document check merely parses a V2 record and copies its key ID. A tampered or untrusted signed record, paired with a document rendered from that record, can therefore be reported conformant. The check path should accept trust keys and apply the same fail-closed verification contract as generation.

Generation renders an AppliedApproval with target.reviewed_digest, whereas checking reconstructs the same overlay with target.digest. These fields represent different artifacts, so a document produced by generate with an approval can be declared drifted by check using the identical inputs and record.

The parsed versioned trace initial state is passed to Monitor::from_state only when Monitor::new fails. When Monitor::new succeeds, replay starts from the model-selected initial state and merely compares it with the trace snapshot, rejecting valid alternative initial states instead of replaying from the state declared by the trace.
